answer.rationale:
The two measured declines this quarter are activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%), and the inherited record most directly addressed to both is memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value), reinforced by memory_31 (fewer required signup fields lifted first-week activation). Fixing the funnel treats the likely cause rather than buying around it, and the gains it produced were described as durable, which matches the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

I am deliberately not chasing promotional_pricing despite the competitor's entry pricing, because memory_73 is the weakest-supported of the tempting options: its own record flags a 12-week observation window and an unchanged support model. A 31% conversion and 18% revenue lift measured over 12 weeks cannot distinguish durable revenue from pulled-forward or discount-anchored revenue, and price-led acquisition in a low-touch segment characteristically degrades cohort quality, retention, and expansion after the promotional period — i.e. it risks trading long-term qualified revenue for a short-term number while also inviting a margin race with a competitor who chose that ground. The unchanged support model also means the test never observed whether a larger, cheaper cohort remains servable at the same quality. That is the downstream value risk I am flagging.

I am spending both verification pulls on memory_73 and memory_86: memory_73 because it is the option whose apparent strength is most likely to be an artifact of a short window and would be the most expensive mistake, and memory_86 because it is the basis of my intended action and I should not commit the only slot this week on an archived summary without checking the original record (effect size, segment, whether the lift persisted, and whether "shortening" traded completion against downstream qualification). If verification shows memory_86's lift was small, segment-specific, or achieved by dropping steps that were actually qualifying users, I would shift to activation_messaging (memory_91), which is the lower-risk in-product lever against the same declines. Referral incentives (memory_57) address established customers, not the failing top of funnel; enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) is sound but targets a segment that is not the source of this quarter's loss and would not move activation.

Scale is a standard experiment rather than a broad rollout: the inherited evidence is from a different quarter and a pre-competitor market, so conditions have changed and the prior effect sizes should be treated as hypotheses to re-measure, not as settled facts. I will hold out a control and instrument downstream qualified-revenue and retention metrics, not just completion rate, so that a completion lift that produces worse accounts is visible rather than counted as success.
